memory_candidates.content: A dispatch-file composer's section ORDER is a correctness property, not cosmetic: a directive meant to constrain how a later section's work is verified must be emitted BEFORE that section, or a top-down reader will act on the later section first. When fixing this, pin the new relative ORDER (not just presence) with a numeric grep -n line-comparison fixture, and prove it with a negative control (temporarily revert the composer, confirm the new assertion actually fails, then restore and re-verify byte-identical).

A crude regex-based lint that counts literal string occurrences of a function name (e.g. a MISSING_DECLARATION check counting 'common_test_resolve_subject' vs 'common_test_declare_subject' occurrences) can be false-positived by a mere PROSE COMMENT mentioning the function name stylistically, with no actual call. When adding comments near code that's subject to such a lint, avoid literal mentions of the gated function/pattern names; describe the behavior instead of citing the helper by name.

deploy-headless.sh runs an inline 'verify-deploy.sh --skip-slow' (the full gate aggregator) by DEFAULT unless --skip-verify is passed. When a task's own subject matter is avoiding full-aggregator contention under a multi-task batch (a Batch Gate Deferral directive), always pass --skip-verify to deploy-headless.sh and follow with the dispatch's own named scoped narrowing instead -- forgetting this flag silently runs the exact full-aggregator-under-contention case the task may be trying to prevent.
